props.title: An eye test, but ==for your website==.
props.subtitle: Point it at a page. Get a friendly report card on how it actually looks to real people.

slides.notes: Welcome. Happy Sight Checker is an eye test for websites — it tells you what your site looks like through the eyes of a real visitor, in plain language.

props.title: Sites quietly ship things ==real visitors struggle to see==.
props.body: Washed-out contrast. Tiny tap targets. Text over busy photos. And when audits catch it, they report it in jargon nobody acts on.

slides.notes: Everyone has shipped a button they couldn't read in sunlight. The tools see it, but they speak in WCAG codes — so the fixes never happen.

props.label: What it does
props.title: A scan that sees ==how your site actually looks==.
props.body: Point it at a page and it flags sight problems in plain, cheerful language — each one with the fix attached.

slides.notes: No spreadsheets of violations. It reads like a friendly note from someone who looked at your site and wants it to do well.

items.title: Contrast
items.body: Can every word actually be read against its background?

items.title: Legibility
items.body: Is the text big, clear, and sitting on busy photos safely?

items.title: Sizing
items.body: Are buttons and tap targets comfortable for real fingers?

items.title: Spacing
items.body: Is there room to breathe, or is everything crowded together?

items.title: Report card
items.body: A short, friendly write-up instead of a spreadsheet of violations.

slides.notes: Four checks plus the write-up. It's the eye chart, not the fine print: the basics that decide whether a page is comfortable to look at.

left.label: Old-school audits
left.title: A to-do list you dread
points: All pass or fail, no nuance
Fixes buried in the fine print

right.label: Happy Sight Checker
right.title: A nudge from a friend
points: "This heading gets shy on dark backgrounds — try a lighter grey"

slides.notes: This is the soul of the product. Accessibility framed as hospitality: welcoming people in, not failing a compliance exam.

tiles.title: Plain-language findings
tiles.body: Every issue explained like a person, with the fix attached.

tiles.title: Prioritized fixes
tiles.body: The most-visible problems surface first — no triage required.

tiles.title: Pass list
tiles.body: A cheerful rundown of what your site is already getting right.

tiles.title: Page-level report card
tiles.body: A short, scannable scorecard instead of a 40-page PDF.

tiles.title: Open source
tiles.body: Read it, run it, fork it — the whole scanner is on GitHub.

tiles.title: Live in your browser
tiles.body: No install, no dashboard to learn. Paste a URL and go.

slides.notes: The feature sweep. Emphasize plain language and the pass list — those are what make people come back instead of dreading it.

stats.label: Live now
stats.caption: Try it on any page — paste a URL and get the report card.

stats.label: Setup time
stats.caption: No account, no install — the scanner is the page.

stats.label: This deck, too
stats.caption: Dark theme, clear-sky accent — it practises what it preaches.

slides.notes: It's shipped and public — not a demo. Point at the live URL, then note that the tool itself is open source.
